paper.title: Software for generation of classes of test functions with known local and global minima for global optimization
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 29(4), 469-480 (TOMS 829, Dec 2003)

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 829.gz (downloaded 2026-11-26, 183683 bytes compressed, 614455 bytes uncompressed; sha256 not recorded by scout)
code.note: Shell archive with C/Dp/Drivers (Makefile, example.c, README, test001 and test001.txt, lmin001, deriv009.txt) and C/Dp/Src (gkls.c, gkls.h, rnd_gen.c, rnd_gen.h). example.c (main, line 181 of the uncompressed text) generates a class of 100 D-type test functions with default parameters and writes the function information to files. The shipped test001.txt is the output for 'D-type function number 1' of that class, dimension 2. Its seed is set in gkls.c by the function that initializes the random sequence (about lines 11167-11185 of the uncompressed text: seed = (nf-1) + (nmin-1)*100 + dim*1000000), so the generator is deterministic. The rerun must check which call in example.c produced test001.txt before running. The paper (ACM DL) has not been read by scout.

claim.location: The shipped reference output test001.txt in C/Dp/Drivers. It lists 'D-type function number 1' with problem dimension 2 and 10 local minimizers. The global minimizer is 'number of the global minimizer is: 2', and its line reads 'f[2] = f( -0.136  0.824) = -1.000; rho[2] = 0.333'.
claim.metric: The coordinates of the global minimizer (local minimizer number 2, the one with f = -1) of D-type function number 1 in dimension 2, as printed by the generator in test001.txt, compared with (-0.136, 0.824).
claim.paper_value: Shipped test001.txt: f[2] = f( -0.136  0.824) = -1.000. The paper's own tables have not been read, so no paper value is used.

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. test001.txt prints coordinates to 3 decimals, so the rounding of the shipped value is up to 5e-4 per coordinate. 1e-3 absolute allows that rounding plus a small margin for compiler or libm differences. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute: the generator for one function of dimension 2 is small. Generating the full 100-function class takes longer but is still well under an hour.
cost.data_size: None; all parameters are hardwired or generated.
cost.data_licence: No data. Netlib TOMS code under the archive's ACM licence; the rerun should record the licence text it finds in the archive.

why: A deterministic test-function generator whose shipped output prints a generated global minimizer location with its radius of attraction; the value needs the generator's random sequence and construction to reproduce, and it has no closed form.
